title: 1915 Portuguese legislative election
summary: Portugal voted on 13 June 1915, a month after the rising of 14 May had thrown out Pimenta de Castro’s government and restored the parliamentary Republic by force. The Democratic Party won 106 of the 163 seats in the Chamber and 45 of the 69 in the Senate, the clearest majority any party held under the 1911 constitution. That majority was also the parliamentary base of intervention: the Democrats were the party that wanted Portugal in the war on Britain’s side, and it was a Democratic government that requisitioned the German ships lying in Portuguese harbours in February 1916, which brought the German declaration of war a fortnight afterwards. It is in the atlas for that consequence rather than for the count.
